newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms on futures but trade muted.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms on futures but trade muted.

text.p: NWE gas oil strengthened slightly on Monday but mainly on the back of benchmark IPE gas oil futures rather than strong fundamentals, traders said.
June IPE gas oil settled $1.50 higher at $174 a tonne.
Heating oil barges traded at June IPE $1.0 and $1.25 fob Rotterdam for first half delivery and premiums were generally talked in the $1.0/$1.75 fob ARA range.

Low sulphur continued to be pressured as arbitraged Mediterranean material moved into the market. Med players said the flow of material northward had left their market rather tight and consequently prices there were tightening but not enough to close the arbitrage door.
Low sulphur premiums were generally quoted at around June IPE +$8.50/+$10 fob ARA, and 3,000 tonnes was done at $8.75 fob Rotterdam early on.
Traders said the market had been fairly quiet throughout the day in typically staid Monday trade.
Also, the strength of the dollar following the victory of the French Socialists in the parliamentary election was also seen weighing on trade.
At 1738 GMT, dollar/mark stood at 1.7299/09 against 1.7082/92 seen in Europe late on Friday. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
